args.body:
PRIORITIZED ISSUES MEMORANDUM
Stipulation of Facts Markup Analysis — Carried Interest Tax Court Dispute
IRS Counterparty Markup of Proposed Stipulation of Facts

MATTER: Tax — Carried Interest Tax Court Dispute
DELIVERABLE: stipulation-markup-analysis.docx

----------------------------------------------------------------------
I. SCOPE AND GOVERNING INSTRUCTIONS
----------------------------------------------------------------------
This memorandum analyzes the IRS's counterparty markup of our proposed
stipulation of facts in the carried interest Tax Court dispute. The
analysis reconciles the IRS markup (Counterparty Markup) against (i) our
base stipulation materials (Matter File 24), (ii) the applicable disclosure
schedules and exhibits (Schedule 3.7, Schedule 5.2, and Exhibit B), and
(iii) the controlling client instruction on issue priorities.

Controlling client instruction (per the latest deal-team message): The
client will CONCEDE the basket conversion, but treats ANY reduction of the
survival period as a WALK-AWAY issue. Earlier messages in the thread stated
the opposite priority ordering; only the latest controlling message governs
this analysis.

The unrelated administrative correspondence misfiled into the matter folder
was identified as a distractor and was NOT relied on.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
II. SUMMARY OF THE IRS MARKUP DEVIATIONS
----------------------------------------------------------------------
The IRS markup accepts most firm-standard provisions but introduces four
material deviations against our base stipulation:

(1) Indemnification cap — silently reduced;
(2) Basket conversion — converted from a deductible basket to a tipping
    basket (i.e., once the basket threshold is reached, liability runs
    dollar-for-dollar from the first dollar rather than only the excess);
(3) Material Adverse Effect (MAE) definition — adds carve-outs for
    regulatory action of exactly the kind at issue in this dispute; and
(4) Limitation period / survival — a new limitation period shortens the
    survival of the core representations.

Each deviation must be reconciled against the base materials and the
governing disclosure schedules before a recommendation can be finalized.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
III. ISSUE-BY-ISSUE ANALYSIS AND RECOMMENDATIONS (PRIORITIZED)
----------------------------------------------------------------------

PRIORITY 1 — WALK-AWAY ISSUE: LIMITATION-PERIOD / SURVIVAL REDUCTION
----------------------------------------------------------------------
The IRS markup introduces a new limitation period that shortens the
survival period for the core representations.

Analysis: Exhibit B to our base materials establishes the survival
matrix. The IRS markup's limitation-period change DIRECTLY CONTRADICTS
Exhibit B. Under the controlling client instruction, any reduction of the
survival period is a walk-away issue. This is the highest-priority item and
must be treated as non-negotiable.

Recommendation: REJECT the IRS's shortened limitation period in its
entirety. Restore the survival matrix exactly as set forth in Exhibit B.
Any survival-period reduction, however modest, is a deal-breaker for the
client and must not be conceded. This is a walk-away issue. Do not trade
any portion of the survival period for other concessions.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
PRIORITY 2 — SILENT INDEMNIFICATION CAP REDUCTION (RECONCILED AGAINST
SCHEDULE 5.2)
----------------------------------------------------------------------
The IRS markup silently reduces the indemnification cap.

Analysis: Schedule 5.2 lists retained liabilities that the markup's
indemnification changes would silently shift onto the client. Because the
cap reduction is made "silently," it has not been negotiated or the subject
of informed client consent. The Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities are
precisely the items that would be left unprotected, or shifted in risk, by
a reduced cap. This is a real risk-transfer deviation that must be
surfaced rather than absorbed.

The client has NOT conceded this item (only the basket conversion was
conceded). Accordingly, it must be flagged for confirmation.

Recommendation: REJECT the silent cap reduction and require the cap be
restored to the level in the base stipulation. Affirmatively confirm that
the Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities remain covered and are not silently
shifted by the reduced cap. Flag to the client that this item, unlike the
basket conversion, has not been conceded and remains a negotiated point.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
PRIORITY 3 — MAE CARVE-OUTS FOR REGULATORY ACTION (RECONCILED AGAINST
SCHEDULE 3.7)
----------------------------------------------------------------------
The IRS markup adds carve-outs to the Material Adverse Effect definition
for regulatory action of exactly the kind at issue in this matter.

Analysis: Schedule 3.7 discloses two pending regulatory inquiries that
intersect these MAE carve-outs. The carve-outs are not innocuous boilerplate
— they are targeted to exclude regulatory action that is squarely relevant
here, and the Schedule 3.7 inquiries are the concrete instance of that risk.
The scheduled exception (Schedule 3.7) controls over any general statement
in the base materials. Because the carve-outs neutralize the very regulatory
exposure that Schedule 3.7 discloses, accepting them would materially
weaken the stipulation's protections.

Recommendation: REJECT the MAE regulatory-action carve-outs, or, at
minimum, narrow them so that they do not capture the two pending regulatory
inquiries disclosed on Schedule 3.7. Retain MAE protections that cover the
regulatory exposure identified in Schedule 3.7. Do not permit the carve-outs
to operate as an indirect indemnification or survival reduction.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
CONCEDED ISSUE — BASKET CONVERSION (DEDUCTIBLE TO TIPPING)
----------------------------------------------------------------------
The IRS markup converts the basket from a deductible to a tipping basket.

Analysis: Under the controlling client instruction, the client has
conceded the basket conversion and does not wish to contest this point.

Recommendation: ACCEPT the basket conversion as conceded by the client.
Confirm that, on a going-forward basis, the stipulation documents this
tipping-basket treatment consistently, and ensure the conversion is limited
to the basket structure only and does not interact with, or contradict, the
survival matrix in Exhibit B or the indemnification cap restored per
Priority 2 above. While the concession is accepted, confirm it is cabined so
it does not silently expand any other liability.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
IV. CROSS-CUTTING RECONCILIATION NOTE
----------------------------------------------------------------------
The disclosure schedules control over general statements in the base
materials. Reconciliation of the IRS markup against BOTH the base materials
and the schedules confirms three live, material deviations (survival
reduction, cap reduction, and MAE carve-outs) plus one conceded deviation
(basket conversion).

- Exhibit B controls the survival matrix (Priority 1 — walk-away).
- Schedule 5.2 controls retained liabilities implicated by the cap change
  (Priority 2).
- Schedule 3.7 controls the pending regulatory inquiries implicated by the
  MAE carve-outs (Priority 3).

The basket conversion (conceded) must not be allowed to bleed into, or
contradict, any of the three live issues above.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
V. ACTIONS AND NEXT STEPS
----------------------------------------------------------------------
1. Reject the shortened limitation period and restore Exhibit B's survival
   matrix (walk-away; non-negotiable).
2. Reject the silent cap reduction; restore the base cap and confirm
   Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities remain covered; flag for client
   confirmation as not conceded.
3. Reject or narrow the MAE regulatory-action carve-outs so they do not
   capture the Schedule 3.7 pending inquiries.
4. Accept the basket conversion as conceded, cabined so it does not alter
   the survival matrix, cap, or MAE coverage.

A redline response to the IRS, incorporating the foregoing positions, should
be prepared and returned to deal team for review.
